newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai sees unemployment rising in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai sees unemployment rising in 1996.

text.p: Shanghai's unemployment will reach 250,000 by the end of 1996, up from 200,000 at the end of 1995, Mayor Xy Kuangdi told a news conference on Monday.
From 1992 to the end of 1995, 870,000 people lost their jobs from traditional state factories and 670,000 of them were re-trained, he said.
Shanghai's resident population at the end of 1995 was 14.15 million, official figures show.
In a speech at the end of a meeting of the International Business Leaders' Advisory Council on Monday, Xu said Shanghai was under heavy unemployment pressure.
He said the service sector was unable to generate enough work for those being laid off from the textile and other light industrial factories in the state sector.
Of those laid off, women account for 70 percent, with 66 percent between 35 and 44, the Liberation Daily on Monday.
The International Business Leaders' Advisory Council meets once a year to advise the Shanghai city government.
